label: Divorce legalization year
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = a curated table of 12 countries, one row each, every row citing the Wikipedia article it was read from (read 2026-10-14) and the statement it relies on. Low: the source is a secondary compilation (Wikipedia), not the statute itself, rows were assembled by hand from article text, and only the countries where divorce was legalized in the 20th century have a row. Countries where divorce has been available since the 19th century or earlier (France, the United Kingdom, Germany, the Nordic countries...) have no single legalization date and are ABSENT; the Philippines and the Vatican, where divorce is not legal, are absent too. No witness tier: no machine-readable door carries the series (probed 2026-10-14).
license: Facts with citation (small extracts, clearly attributed) - see docs/licenses.md and catalog/curated/README.md.
notes: Start of the legal availability of divorce in the regime still in force (decision 24). Source: the list 'countries that have relatively recently legalized divorce' of Wikipedia's Divorce article (Italy 1970, Portugal 1975, Brazil 1977, Spain 1981, Argentina 1987, Paraguay 1991, Colombia 1991, Andorra 1995, Ireland 1996, Chile 2004, Malta 2011) plus Panama 1911 from the Divorce law by country table. HONEST LIMITS: 12 countries, a deliberately small set; the Andorra date is not cross-checked; Paraguay is 1992 in the other table.
